comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
The 0.8.0 observation pass settled the API half (docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 5).

Decided: encoding is daemon-side. herdr exposes no pane terminal modes anywhere in its API, and the frame stream consumes the sequences that set them, so neither the surface nor the adapter can encode. terminal.input takes raw bytes; herdr's raw_input parses them and re-encodes for the pane's modes, which is what its own TUI relies on. Muster reports bytes.

Ruled out: pane.send_keys. It refuses home, end, pageup, pagedown, insert, delete, and ctrl+alt+delete with invalid_key - a named-key API with no navigation cluster cannot carry a terminal keyboard.

Still open, and why this card stays in next: IME composition, AltGr, dead keys, and whether byte-level reporting preserves enough for the kitty protocol in practice. All need the Swift surface, so this is blocked behind the libghostty spike rather than behind more daemon observation.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
The renderer half is now settled too, and it lands better than expected: herdr re-encodes input with libghostty-vt's own key encoder (src/ghostty/mod.rs:2547 and :2552 call ghostty_key_encoder_setopt_from_terminal and _encode). Muster can encode with the same library, so the path is ghostty-encode, herdr's crossterm parse, ghostty-encode - one foreign step between two runs of one engine, not two implementations that have to agree.

Correcting the plan's wording: do NOT encode at maximal fidelity. herdr's TUI enables exactly three kitty flags - disambiguate, report event types, report alternate keys (src/input/model.rs:219) - and the function is called ime_compatible_keyboard_enhancement_flags because reporting all keys as escape codes breaks IME. src/input/model.rs:427 asserts REPORT_ALL_KEYS stays out. Match those three.

Still needs the Swift surface: IME composition, AltGr, dead keys. The key event struct carries a 'composing' flag, so the shape is there.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Pane terminal modes (kitty keyboard, bracketed paste, mouse reporting) live in the daemon's VT and are not replayed in the frame stream, so surfaces cannot encode input. Candidates: daemon-side encoding (send-keys style API) or adapter-side encoding from exposed mode state (may need an upstream herdr PR - their own TUI client reports maximal key info and lets the server encode). Test kitty protocol, IME, AltGr, mouse, paste. Stage-1 gate: no faithful input path means the architecture fails.
title: Input path: prove daemon-side-correct encoding
